extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, investigators, and students of empirical method (readers learning Baconian method for inquiry)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for collecting, classifying, and using different kinds of empirical 'instances' (examples, experiments, prodigies) to discover forms and causes in natural philosophy. Emphasizes types of instances, how to use them to decide between hypotheses, and how to compile credible natural histories as preparation for experimental work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deviating instances (errors of nature / monstrous objects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deviating instances are errors of nature or strange and monstrous objects in which nature deviates from her ordinary course; they differ from singular instances in being miracles of individuals rather than species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to rectify the understanding distorted by habit and to reveal common forms. Do not desist from inquiry until the cause of the deviation is discerned; the cause may point to a latent process rather than a regular form. They are especially apt for practice and the operative branch (variation of known species is easier than generating new species). Compile a particular natural history of monsters and prodigies (new, rare, unusual) with rigorous selection; prefer grave and credible histories and faithful narration; beware of superstition and writers of natural magic/alchemy as they often contain fables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bordering instances (participants / intermediate forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances exhibiting species that appear composed of two species or that are rudiments between one and another (things ‘between’ established species).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Class these with singular or heteroclite instances but treat them separately because they point out order and constitution of things and suggest causes for the number and quality of common species. Use them to lead the understanding from what is to what is possible (examples: moss between putrescence and plant; comets between stars and meteors; flying fishes; bats).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instances of power (fasces / wit or hands of man / masterpieces of art)
rubrics_metrics.description: Works most noble and perfect—the masterpieces of every art, i.e., human works in which power has been most fully realized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine mechanical and practical liberal arts and compile the great masterpieces and the modes of effecting them; from such works it is often easier to advance, adapt, or apply to new purposes. Beware that wondrous works of art can 'depress' or 'chain' the understanding—do not suppose nothing similar can be achieved without the same means. Note that many great discoveries arise not by gradual improvement of arts but by invention of forms; nevertheless, study of arts can guide invention. Include singular instances of art (e.g., paper) and prefer artificial works that imitate nature or powerfully govern/change her course. Do not wholly despise charms/conjuring or superstition—investigate them to see if latent natural operations exist (e.g., fascination, sympathy, transmission of impressions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective preparative compilation of certain instances
rubrics_metrics.description: The similar, singular, deviating, bordering instances, and those of power should be collected together as a particular history to prepare and correct the understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a single compilation of these five species at once (not reserved per nature) to arrange matter entering the understanding and correct habitual corruption. Use them as a preparative to purify the intellect and to level it for reception of true notions; these instances also prepare the way for practical (operative) investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accompanying and hostile instances (instances for fixed propositions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accompanying instances are concretes where the required nature is constantly found as an inseparable companion; hostile instances are concretes where the required nature is constantly avoided and excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From these derive certain and universal propositions (affirmative or negative) about concretes and predicates. Use accompanying instances to narrow the affirmative of form (and hostile instances to define negatives). Note two important points: (1) If no universal affirmative/negative exists, carefully note its non-existence; (2) For general propositions, subjoin concretes approaching nearest to the non-existing substance to show limits of existence (e.g., flame as accompanying instance of heat; air as hostile instance of solidity). Particular exceptions may be allowed if singular/rare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjunctive instances (instances of extremity or limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances indicating extremes, limits, or measures—instances which show 'how far' nature effects or allows anything.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exemplars of maximum or minimum (e.g., gold in weight, iron in hardness, whale in size of animals, dog in smell, flame of gunpowder in rapid expansion; and defects like spirits of wine in lightness, worms upon the skin in animal size) to indicate divisions of nature, measures, and boundaries. Include extremes in defect as well as abundance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instances of alliance or union
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances where heterogeneous natures mingle or unite, showing that an operation characteristic of one nature may be attributed to another, proving differences may be modifications of a common nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use alliance instances to elevate thought from differences to genera and remove deceptive images. Experimentally show how one nature can be made to resemble another (example: fire modified to imitate the sun's heat). Analyze the real differences (e.g., four differences between solar heat and fire: degree, quality/moisture, inequality in time, and duration/impatience of effect) and seek ways to modify conditions (temper, humidity, inequality, duration) to bring one effect into resemblance with another. Provide concrete experimental arrangements and examples (vine branch ripening near fire; eggs hatched by fire; revival of benumbed butterflies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instances of the cross (decisive / judicial / oracle instances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisive instances used when the understanding is balanced between two or more candidate causes; they show that one nature’s union with the required nature is firm and the other's is separable, thus deciding between hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek or design instances (often new and purposely sought) that decisively reject or confirm one hypothesis over another. Apply to concrete problems by reducing possibilities and devising observations/experiments whose outcomes are possible only under one hypothesis (examples/guidance provided: tides—check simultaneous floods on opposite coasts and Southern Ocean/isthmus observations; whether tide is progressive or due to rising from bottom; examine curvature of sea surface during ebb/flood by sounding; diurnal motion—look for east-west motion in ocean/air/low comets/planets and compare speeds; weight/gravity—clock experiments at height vs deep mines to test attraction by corporeal mass; magnetism—magnetic globe polarity experiment). Use these cross instances to terminate and complete an interpretation when they decisively favor one cause; if inconclusive, pursue other cross instances.
